title: Regenerate docs/design/js-module-index.md and close the contract gap

sections.what: docs/design/js-module-index.md is stale against the source it is generated from. It lists 382 modules / 211 documented / 171 awaiting a contract header; a live run of `python tools/js_module_index.py --write` reports 405 / 223 / 182. The missing rows are real modules added since the index was last generated, including static/js/agent/prompt-builder/capture.js (the shared turn-prompt capture used by the Benchmark Lab and the in-app harness). It cannot be regenerated today without reintroducing banned characters: roughly 100 source headers still use an em-dash (-) as their separator, and the generator emits that character verbatim into the Powers column, which violates the repo-wide em-dash ban.
sections.why: The index is a generated reference, not a hand-written note, so the drift is a bug in the declaration, not a documentation gap to paper over. Leaving it stale means every new module is invisible in the index until someone hand-edits it, which the file's own header forbids. The em-dash blocker is the same sweep as bug-564 (Way Properties.md carries 117 em-dashes) and is not being fixed here; this task exists so the index regeneration is not silently blocked by it.
sections.how: 1. Make the generator em-dash-proof: in tools/js_module_index.py write_index(), normalise the em-dash and en-dash characters to an ASCII hyphen in every emitted cell before writing the markdown, so regenerating can never reintroduce a banned character. 2. Run `python tools/js_module_index.py --write` and confirm the diff is only the missing rows plus the normalised separators. 3. Update the baseline if the two currently-uncovered modules (static/js/ui/play-mode.js, static/js/ui/source-version.js) are intentionally left undocumented. 4. Add the @module/@contributes headers to play-mode.js and source-version.js if they are meant to be documented, or record them in docs/design/js-module-baseline.txt.
